catalog_quote: 2.5 Prosody 2.5.1 Stress Stress is not distinctive in 'Ôrôê. In words, it generally falls on the penultimate syllable. The syllables that receive stress are underlined: ai “to marry” ighù “to cook” nene “fire” puie “to open” avavoa “ladybug” When the word final is long vowel, the stress falls on the last vowel. pèèrii “to roll” jouu “waterfall” maimii “hungry” [p. 4:] Long vowels corresponding to each short vowel are also found, except for long vowels corresponding to /ỹ/ and /ẽ/. new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and falls on the penultimate syllable; if the word ends in a long vowel (written as a doubled vowel, syllable structure (C)V), stress falls on that final long vowel instead. Equivalently, stress on the penultimate vowel/mora counting a final long vowel as two.
new_statements.exceptions: Words ending in a long vowel take final stress (pèèrii, jouu, maimii). 'Generally' penultimate otherwise; no lexical exceptions listed. Underlining marking the stressed syllables in the examples is lost in the text layer but visible in the PDF.
new_statements.domain_note: Stated for words ('In words, it generally falls...'), i.e. citation forms; sentence-level pitch treated separately under 2.5.2 Intonation (content words receive higher pitch). Language is not described as tonal.
new_statements.identity_note: Tsuji 2014 describes 'Ôrôê (Orowe, bpk = orow1242) as spoken in the tribus of Pothé, Azareu, Ny and Bouirou, commune of Bourail; self-designation /ʔõɾõe/, also called 'the language of Bourail'. No dialect restriction stated; same variety as the Glottolog languoid.

sources.note: Sec. 2.5.1 (p.5): stress is not distinctive; generally penultimate syllable in words (examples ai, ighù, nene, puie, avavoa); when the word ends in a long vowel, stress falls on that last (long) vowel (pèèrii, jouu, maimii). Sec. 2.5.2 covers sentence intonation (content words get higher pitch). Also p.3: schwa 'tends to be slightly rounded when it appears in a stressed syllable'.
